newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar opens weaker on soft inflation data.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar opens weaker on soft inflation data.

text.p: * Canada's dollar opened weaker at C$1.3870 (US$0.7209) in light trading on Tuesday after Statistics Canada reported softer-than-expected consumer price data for May, traders said. * They said the absence of inflationary pressures in the Canadian economy would ease pressure on the Bank of Canada to tighten monetary policy in the upcoming months.
"Unfortunately, this may contribute a little bit more to the Canadian dollar's woes," said Michael Gregory, economist and strategist with Lehman Brothers.
"People are expecting the Bank of Canada to push back that point where they first tighten, and this number today would suggest that they are not going to be in any hurry," Gregory added.

Analysts said currency markets would keep a close eye on U.S. inflation data due to be released this morning at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT. A Reuter survey of economists forecast consumer prices in May rose 0.2 percent.
A stronger-than-expected U.S. inflation number, however, may not be enough to push the U.S. Federal Reserve to raise interest rates at its next Federal Open Market Committee meeting on July 1-2.

"We'll wait and see what the U.S. numbers bring us," said Reid Farrill, corporate foreign exchange adviser for CIBC Wood Gundy. "Given the fact that last week's numbers were on the soft side, I don't think the market is expecting any major change."
"Any inflationary numbers would probably surprise the market," Farrill said.
On the crosses, the Canada dollar climbed to 81.87 from Monday's 81.63 and rose to 1.2510 marks from Monday's 1.2487 marks.
